topChanges.title: 1. Collapse authoring to single-file features with auto-wiring (goal 1's make-or-break change)
topChanges.what: Kill the 4-way split (contract.ts / operations.ts / feature.ts / application.ts). Let defineCommand/defineQuery own everything for one operation: schemas inline, error codes with HTTP status inline, optional http:{method,path} metadata, and a colocated default adapter binding. Derive FeatureDescriptor automatically — createApplication already computes requiredPorts from operation effects (packages/core/src/application.ts:272-283), so feature.ts's re-listing of operations/ports/events/invariants and defineFeatureContract's untyped exports are pure ceremony; delete them. Generate HTTP routes from operation metadata so a new endpoint edits ONE file. This must land FIRST: the compiler scanner (packages/compiler/src/scanner.ts:519-989 keys on defineFeature literals), the scaffold, the docs, and both benchmark arms all depend on the authoring shape. Verified today: adding one endpoint touches 4-6 files (~1,000 LOC context) in examples/framework-app and 6 files in sandbox/notes-app vs 3 for the Express arm — the framework currently INVERTS its own headline goal, and one error code (CUSTOMER_ALREADY_EXISTS) is declared in 7 places across 3 files. Note: this requires consciously revising docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:19-30, whose principles ('all registration through explicit values', 'concision that hides registration is rejected') are the root cause of the ceremony — the overhaul fights the documented design until that doc changes.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Add-an-endpoint drops from 4-6 files to 1-2 (operation file + test); read context for a typical change drops from ~10-14k tokens to ~2-4k; sandbox change-cost flips from worse-than-Express (6 writes vs 3) to better (2 vs 3); error-code declarations collapse from 7 sites to 1-2.
topChanges.risk: Medium: breaking API change (fine pre-1.0); scanner must be rewritten in lockstep or inspect/affected/verify silently degrade; examples/shared-contract acceptance suite (1,133 LOC, npm run test:acceptance) must keep passing to prove behavior parity survived.

topChanges.title: 2. Production fast path in core dispatch: cache per-operation machinery, conditional trace, mode-gated re-validation
topChanges.what: Three verified per-dispatch wastes in packages/core/src/application.ts: (a) buildEffects/buildEmitter rebuild sorted alias lists, an always-satisfied declaredIds Set, 2 closures per effect, and frozen contexts on EVERY dispatch (l.482-682) — precompute the handler table per operation at createApplication and parameterize only lifecycle+trace; (b) trace entries are constructed, frozen, and pushed unconditionally (l.605-613, 675-678) then discarded by includeTrace when tracing is off — pass traceEnabled down and skip construction; (c) operation output, effect outputs, and error details are fully re-parsed on every completion regardless of mode (l.750-829) — in mode 'production' skip effect-output and operation-output re-parsing (keep input validation and error-code membership checks), keep full validation in development/test. Also: accept ReadonlySet principal.permissions to avoid new Set per dispatch (l.360), and cut schema allocations ([...path,key] spreads at schema.ts:274, per-parse Object.keys(source).sort() at schema.ts:279 — note shape keys ARE already presorted at creation, schema.ts:243, so only the unexpected-key scan needs fixing).
topChanges.expectedEffect: Dispatch overhead from ~2.0µs toward the plain-TS ~0.9µs baseline (smoke data); removes a large slice of the 74µs gap vs Express; per-system retained RSS (currently 12.7x plain) shrinks as closures/frozen wrappers disappear.
topChanges.risk: Medium: dev/prod divergence — adapter bugs that dev catches (invalid effect output) pass silently in production; mitigate by keeping error-path validation always-on and offering opt-in sampling. Trace-off paths need test coverage so lifecycle faults still latch correctly.

topChanges.title: 3. Rewrite the Node HTTP hot path: bucketed routing, deferred body read, single permission check, fewer copies
topChanges.what: All verified in packages/adapters-http: (a) handler.ts:121-127 flatMaps matchPath over EVERY route per request (405 support), re-splitting the same pathname per candidate (l.34) and re-uppercasing the method inside find (l.126) — bucket routes by method at compileRoutes, index static paths in a Map, split the path once, compute Allow lazily on miss; sort param routes static-first to fix the registration-order /users/:id-shadows-/users/me hazard (compileRoutes l.60-76 only rejects identical shapes); (b) delete the duplicate permission pre-check (handler.ts:162-179) — core repeats it identically at application.ts:360-378 and the adapter already maps rejected PERMISSION_DENIED to 403; (c) node.ts:97 buffers up to 1MiB of body BEFORE routing/auth (perf + unauthenticated DoS) — defer body reading until a route matches and the principal resolves; (d) fix the double body copy (node.ts:66 Uint8Array.from(Buffer.concat(...))) and the response triple round-trip (string → Response → await arrayBuffer() → Buffer, node.ts:81) by carrying the pre-stringified payload; (e) longer-term, add a raw req/res Node host that skips undici Request construction entirely, keeping the Web handler as the edge entry. Add an onError hook — the catch-alls at handler.ts:209-218 and node.ts:118-127 currently swallow errors with zero observability.
topChanges.expectedEffect: This layer is where most of the 74µs-vs-Express gap lives (core dispatch is only ~1-2µs of it). Realistic outcome: at-or-below Express median latency, competitive with Fastify on static routes; removes a memory-DoS vector; fixes a real routing correctness bug.
topChanges.risk: Low-medium: handler.test.ts (353 LOC) covers current semantics; static-first precedence is a deliberate behavior change that needs documenting. The raw-host variant doubles the host surface to maintain.

topChanges.title: 4. Make the benchmark able to prove goal 3 — currently it falsifies it, partly through self-inflicted target overhead
topChanges.what: The only Express/NestJS evidence on record shows Agentix 56% SLOWER (207.4µs vs 133.0µs median, docs/HTTP_FRAMEWORK_BENCHMARK.md:58-70). Three fixes: (a) equalize work — the Express/Nest targets do a minimal finite-number check (targets/express.ts:24 isEchoInput) while Agentix does full dispatch+validation; give Express/Nest arms zod validation (zod 4.4.3 is already a root devDependency) as a second measured condition. Critically, I verified the Agentix target ALSO adds a redundant THIRD validation the maps missed: mapResponse re-runs EchoOutput.safeParse (targets/agentix.ts:71) on output core already validated (application.ts:761) — the measured 207µs overstates framework cost; (b) add a concurrency/throughput mode (N sockets, req/s) and a multi-route + path-param workload — sequential single-socket latency on one echo route cannot support any serving claim; (c) rerun from a clean commit (the frozen run was dirty-worktree, commit 9ab2948) and wire CI regression budgets (dispatch µs, RSS, median latency vs Express) into .github/workflows/benchmark-smoke.yml so changes #2-3 get fast feedback.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Turns goal 3 from 'currently falsified by own data' into a falsifiable, CI-guarded claim; removes ~one full validation pass of measured overhead from the Agentix arm immediately.
topChanges.risk: Low: measurement-only. Preregistration rules forbid touching frozen v1 artifacts — new runs must be new files (append-only results/), which the protocol already supports.

topChanges.title: 5. Make `agentix inspect` the one-artifact change context and fix verify's narrow scope
topChanges.what: Today inspect delivers discovery, not change context: input/output are captured as expression text only ('CreateOrderInput', scanner.ts:770-779), so agents still open 3-5 source files per change. Embed bounded source excerpts (schema/type declaration text ≤1KiB each via the checker already in hand at scanner.ts:569, execute signature, port operation signatures) under the existing 8KiB/omissions mechanism, and index bindPort call sites + defineHttpRoute locations so 'where is this port implemented/exposed' stops requiring the 414-line application.ts (gap admitted in docs/DECISIONS.md D-032). Fix two verified bugs that waste every agent session: (a) planVerification can NEVER produce narrow scope for a root-tsconfig app — the predicate requires resolve(project) !== resolve(rootDir) (packages/compiler/src/affected.ts:250), so verify always runs the whole workspace even with a proven 1-test closure; drop that clause and run the selected test files; (b) ANY unresolved edge anywhere widens ALL affected results to whole-workspace (affected.ts:106-111) — scope widening to the reachable subgraph. Also fix exportedNames dropping `export { a, b }` declarations (scanner.ts:248-268), which zeroes contract.exports for barrel files.
topChanges.expectedEffect: One inspect call (~2-3k tokens) replaces 2-3 file reads per change; verify runs seconds of targeted tests instead of the full workspace — the direct token/time payoff the whole compiler exists for.
topChanges.risk: Low: additive to a bounded artifact with an omissions ledger; the re-analysis-per-invocation design is an explicit trust decision (cli.ts:142-143 comment), so if you also wire the manifest cache, keep the hash-verified staleness check as the gate.

topChanges.title: 6. Delete dead and duplicated API surface: aliases, inert invariants, replay, redundant re-listing
topChanges.what: Prune before 1.0: (a) the 7 alias exports — command/query/event/invariant/feature (descriptors.ts:424-427,479), defineAdapter=bindPort (l.171), defineContract=defineFeatureContract (l.226) — two names per concept doubles what agents must recognize; (b) defineInvariant is registered and id-checked (application.ts:287-293) but NEVER executed by dispatch (verified: those are the only references) — either run invariants after completion in dev/test mode or delete the concept; the current state costs tokens with zero runtime value and the example calls .check() by hand; (c) testing/replay.ts is 293 LOC (a third of @agentix/testing) with no capture bridge from real dispatches and zero usage anywhere — delete it or build captureReplayRecord; (d) compiler likelyAffected (scanner.ts:448-517) is the superlinear term in index.json (283 lines for a 2-operation app) and nothing consumes it — delete; (e) trace-payload boilerplate: type harness results with non-optional trace when trace!==false.
topChanges.expectedEffect: Public surface shrinks ~30%; docs and agent memorization shrink proportionally; index.json drops from 14k chars to a few k for small apps (the verified 3x naive-worst context penalty in the sandbox largely disappears).
topChanges.risk: Low: mechanical breakage in examples/sandbox; invariant execution (if kept) needs a performance-safe dev-only path.

topChanges.title: 7. Ship docs where agents actually are: in-package llms.txt/API.md, split research docs out of docs/
topChanges.what: Published packages ship dist ONLY (verified: packages/core/package.json files: ["dist", ...]) with a 15-line README pointing at GitHub Pages — an agent maintaining an app that installed @agentix/* from npm has ZERO offline docs and must read node_modules dist or the web. Add a compact API.md/llms.txt (every export, one-line signature, one 30-line canonical feature) to each package's files array. In-repo, split docs/ into agent-facing (GETTING_STARTED, CORE_CONCEPTS, API_REFERENCE, CLI, HTTP, TESTING) and docs/research/ (DECISIONS 996 lines, BENCHMARK_PROTOCOL 527, HYPOTHESIS, PHASE5_READINESS, LIMITATIONS — ~50KB of methodology an agent globbing docs/ burns tokens on), and add a single ~150-line AUTHORING.md cheat sheet reflecting the NEW single-file authoring model from change #1.
topChanges.expectedEffect: First-contact cost for a consumer-app agent drops from ~10-20k tokens (reading src/tests) to ~2-3k; repo-local agents stop paying the research-doc glob tax.
topChanges.risk: Near zero; only cost is keeping API.md in sync — generate it from the compiler's own analysis to avoid drift.

topChanges.title: 8. Test fixture factory and HTTP test client in @agentix/testing
topChanges.what: Every test file hand-assembles createApplication + bindPort fakes (28 of 77 lines in the canonical customers.test.ts), forcing a read of contract.ts + feature.ts per test. Add createTestApplication({features, overrides?}) that auto-binds unbound ports to recording fakes and auto-wires deterministic clock/id for port operations with kind 'time'/'random' (the kind metadata already exists on portOperation), returning {application, ports, clock, ids}. Add testHttp(handler, {method, path, body, principal}) wrapping adapters-http's fetch-style createHttpHandler — routing/auth/status mapping is currently untestable without hand-built Request objects (supertest parity gap vs both Express and Nest).
topChanges.expectedEffect: Per-test fixture from ~28 lines to ~3; test authorship stops requiring contract.ts/feature.ts reads (2 fewer file reads per test task); closes the supertest parity gap for goal 4.
topChanges.risk: Low: additive; auto-faking must fail loudly for ports with no schema-derivable default so tests don't silently pass on wrong fakes.

mapErrors: Core map overstates the docs gap for repo-local agents: it claims first contact 'means reading core src (2,024 LOC ≈ ~20k tokens) or the docs/ site', but the repo ships a real in-repo authoring set (docs/GETTING_STARTED.md 355 lines, CORE_CONCEPTS.md 284, API_REFERENCE.md 231, CLI.md 225) plus a root AGENTS.md that is the documented entry point. The genuine gap is different and unmapped: published npm packages ship dist only (packages/core/package.json 'files': ['dist', ...]), so CONSUMER-app agents have zero offline docs — a distinct problem from what the map describes.

Compiler map frames loadFreshIndex re-analysis as an oversight ('no use of the existing checkIndexStaleness/readIndex cache path... dead weight'). It is an explicit, documented design decision: packages/cli/src/cli.ts:142-143 carries the comment 'Generated indexes are disposable outputs, never trusted inputs to agent context', and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:21 states 'Generated metadata is disposable.' The perf opportunity is real, but the fix must answer the stated trust argument (hash-verified staleness as the gate), not just wire readIndex in.

Benchmarks map (and the core/http maps) missed that the measured 207.4µs Agentix latency includes SELF-INFLICTED target overhead beyond framework cost: benchmarks/runtime/src/http-comparison/targets/agentix.ts:71 re-runs EchoOutput.safeParse in mapResponse on output that core dispatch already validated at application.ts:761 — a third validation pass. The documented unequal-work caveat (HTTP_FRAMEWORK_BENCHMARK.md:72-75) understates the asymmetry; part of the 74µs gap is benchmark-target code, not the framework.

Sandbox map claims a contradiction — 'results/README.md claims results are ignored/CI-only, yet token-budget-latest.{json,md} sit in the worktree'. Verified false: git check-ignore confirms sandbox/token-budget/results/token-budget-latest.md IS gitignored; local presence of ignored files is exactly what the README describes. The narrower point (results lack commit/CLI-version stamps for traceability) does stand.

Core map's framing 'there is no capsule concept anywhere in core' reads as a doc/code inconsistency; in fact docs/ARCHITECTURE.md and CORE_CONCEPTS.md define 'capsule' deliberately as an authoring convention, not a runtime construct. Not a factual error, but the map misses the more important conflict: ARCHITECTURE.md:19-30's principles ('all registration through explicit values', 'concision that hides registration is rejected') are the designed-in cause of the ceremony every map complains about — the overhaul must revise that document, not just the code.

Minor: authoring map says CUSTOMER_ALREADY_EXISTS is declared in '7 places across 3 files' — verified exactly right (3 in application.ts, 2 in contract.ts, 2 in operations.ts); and core map's LOC figure (2,024) verified exact. No arithmetic errors found in the numbers I checked — the maps are quantitatively reliable overall.
blindSpots: examples/shared-contract (1,133 LOC: acceptance.ts 866 + index.ts 235) — nobody read it. It is the transport-neutral acceptance suite that BOTH examples/framework-app and examples/plain-app must pass (npm run test:acceptance), i.e., the only mechanism proving the two arms are behaviorally equivalent. Any authoring-model overhaul (change #1) must keep it green, and it is a hidden per-change cost the context walks never counted.

docs/ARCHITECTURE.md — unread by all mappers, yet it contains the framework's actual design objective and principles. Notably it does NOT claim runtime superiority over Express/NestJS (its objective is bounded machine-discoverable maintenance scope), and its explicit-registration principles directly conflict with the owner's goal 1. The overhaul needs a conscious decision to amend this document; otherwise every simplification violates the written architecture.

The publishing/distribution pipeline: packages ship dist-only ('files' arrays), docs are deployed to GitHub Pages via docs/_config.yml + _layouts + .github/workflows/pages.yml, and scripts/ (check-release-packages.mjs, prepare-github-test-release.mjs, mark-binaries-executable.mjs) plus release.yml/changesets govern what consumers receive. Nobody verified what an npm consumer actually sees — which is where the agent-first goals will be judged in the wild.

CI workflows (.github/workflows/ci.yml, benchmark-smoke.yml, github-test-release.yml) — unread. There are currently no perf or context-cost regression gates in CI; the proposed regression budgets (dispatch µs, RSS, latency vs Express, token-budget deltas) have an obvious home here that no map located.

engines: 'node >=24.0.0 <25' pins every package to a single Node major (root and packages' package.json). Express/NestJS support many majors; this is a real general-purpose (goal 4) adoption constraint nobody flagged, and it also narrows where benchmark results generalize.

The compiler's dependency on TypeScript 7.0.2's unstable native sync API ('typescript/unstable/sync') — the compiler map mentions the pin but nobody assessed the risk: the entire inspect/affected/verify chain rests on an explicitly unstable API of a pre-release TS major; an API change strands the CLI. Deserves a compatibility shim or vendored fallback plan.

examples/plain-app was only skimmed (2 files cited). Since it is the fairness baseline for the frozen two-arm study and the 'plain TS is terser' claims, nobody actually verified it is a fair strict-TS equivalent rather than an idealized minimum — e.g., whether it implements the same permission checks, tracing, and validation rigor the framework arm pays for.

vitest.config.ts, tsconfig.base.json/tsconfig.json project-reference topology — unread; they determine whether planVerification's 'project' scope could ever trigger in THIS repo and what 'npm run typecheck' actually costs an agent per verify cycle.

No one examined git history/branch state of this worktree (branch main, clean) against the pending task list (#3 implement, #4/#5 prove) — the overhaul has not started; every map conclusion describes the pre-overhaul baseline, which is the correct baseline but worth stating explicitly.
verdict: Verified against its own code and frozen evidence, Agentix currently achieves none of its four goals — but the gaps are engineering-tractable, not conceptual. Goal 1 (agent-first, 1-2 files) is INVERTED: a typical change touches 4-6 files in the example app and 6 in the sandbox versus 3 for the Express arm, because the capsule split (contract/operations/feature) plus central application.ts wiring multiplies edit sites; this is designed-in (docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's explicit-registration principles), so fixing it is a design revision, not a bug fix. Goal 2 (token efficiency) has zero real measurements and the only heuristic data shows a statistical tie at small scale (872 vs 877 vs 875 est tokens) with Agentix's full-src ~1.9x larger. Goal 3 (beat Express/NestJS) is currently FALSIFIED by the project's own frozen benchmark (207.4µs vs 133.0µs median, +56%), though ~all of the gap lives in fixable places: per-dispatch rebuild/freeze/validate overhead in core (verified at application.ts:360, 482-682, 750-829), a linear-scan buffering Web-Request Node host in adapters-http, and partly the benchmark target itself (a redundant third validation at targets/agentix.ts:71). Goal 4 (NestJS-general) is roughly 60% there — DI lifecycle, middleware/guards equivalents, event subscription, transactions, cancellation, streaming, and schema-library breadth are all missing. The genuinely differentiated assets — the bounded 8KiB inspect artifact, the affected-closure graph, deterministic testing, and total behavioral explicitness of operation descriptors — are real and worth preserving; but they solve discovery, not change-making, and are currently buried under authoring ceremony that costs more than the discovery savings return. Execute changes #1 (single-file authoring) and #2+#3 (dispatch + HTTP fast paths) first, with #4's honest benchmark as the feedback loop; without #1 the framework loses to Express on its own flagship metric at every app size where anyone would evaluate it.
